rationale: Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-015 (illustrative figures), A-1: demand keeps growing about 3% a year, so at the meter rate the fixed fleet falls short of demand within about two years.

No matching assumption in WE-015; judged from the text: licensed cabs on streets and ranks are visible and the Office fines and impounds, so little taxi service takes place beyond the cap; A-7 puts evasion separately.

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-015 (illustrative figures), A-7: unlicensed service and off-meter deals often go undetected (12 inspectors, a large city, pick-up bans on suburban taxis hard to police).

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-015 (illustrative figures), A-9: medallion holders can organize at a cost below their stake (existing drivers' association, concentrated and identifiable gain).
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-015 (illustrative figures), A-3: medallion holders and buyers expect the cap to last.

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-015 (illustrative figures), A-16: the Office's budget rises with the added enforcement work, rather than the 12 inspectors being moved from other duties.
